editor_note: Entry 4 is faithful and natural: "dibangunkan menggunakan keperluan berikut" and "Kami mengesyorkan penggunaan versi ini atau yang lebih baharu" keep the "or newer" meaning of the English.

Rewritten entry 15 is faithful. It keeps "akses eksklusif kepada sistem", "tiada job lain boleh berjalan — termasuk job penentukuran" and the queuing benefit ("mengelakkan kelewatan akibat baris gilir setiap job secara berasingan"), and renders variational as "algoritma variasi", which matches the rest of the file.

The description text in both rewritten cards is accurate and reads naturally. Entry 12 renders "free learning offerings" as "tawaran pembelajaran percuma kami", and entry 13 renders "curated sequences" as "urutan ... yang telah dipilih khas". Neither would mislead a learner. The rewrite did leave some text users see in English, though. In entry 12, linkText "Visit IBM Quantum Learning" was not translated. In entry 13, title "Learning paths" and linkText "Explore learning paths" were not translated. Every other card on the page translates its title and linkText (for example "Tutorial"/"Layari tutorial" and "Pengoptimuman"/"Terokai butiran Transpiler"). The title "Learning" in entry 12 is also untranslated, but it can be defended as the name of the IBM Quantum Learning product.

examples.source: title="Learning paths" ... linkText="Explore learning paths"
examples.translation: title="Learning paths" ... linkText="Explore learning paths"
examples.suggested: title="Laluan pembelajaran" ... linkText="Terokai laluan pembelajaran"
examples.why: This card title and link label are visible to users but were left in English. Sibling cards translate theirs (Tutorial / Layari tutorial), so this card is inconsistent with the rest of the page.

examples.source: linkText="Visit IBM Quantum Learning"
examples.translation: linkText="Visit IBM Quantum Learning"
examples.suggested: linkText="Lawati IBM Quantum Learning"
examples.why: The product name can stay in English, but the verb "Visit" should be translated. Every other card's call-to-action on the page is in Malay.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The migration tables, the rule that num_randomizations * shots_per_randomization takes precedence over shots, the job-splitting example and the local-testing caveats all match the English. A few wording slips remain. In [53], "penstimulasi statevector (hingar)" contains a typo that reads like "stimulator"; it should be "penyimulasi", and "noisy" should be "berhingar", not the noun "hingar". Elsewhere there are several literal calques: "diselesaikan kepada" for "resolve to" [12], "menyiri-alirkan" for "serializes" [40], and "Parameter diikat terus" and "gagal dipaksa" for "bound away" and "fails coercion" [56].

examples.source: A fake backend uses a statevector (noisy) simulator
examples.translation: Backend palsu menggunakan penstimulasi statevector (hingar)
examples.suggested: Backend palsu menggunakan penyimulasi statevector (berhingar)
examples.why: 'penstimulasi' is a typo that reads like 'stimulator'. Also, the noun 'hingar' means 'noise', but the source is the adjective 'noisy', which is 'berhingar'.

examples.source: the top-level imports will resolve to the new client-side implementations
examples.translation: import peringkat atas akan diselesaikan kepada pelaksanaan sisi klien baharu
examples.suggested: import peringkat atas akan merujuk kepada pelaksanaan sisi klien baharu
examples.why: 'diselesaikan' means 'solved/settled'. It is a literal calque of 'resolve' and does not carry the sense of an import pointing to a module.

examples.source: calling it inside the submission loop serializes the jobs
examples.translation: memanggilnya di dalam gelung penghantaran akan menyiri-alirkan kerja tersebut
examples.suggested: memanggilnya di dalam gelung penghantaran akan menyebabkan kerja tersebut dijalankan secara bersiri
examples.why: 'menyiri-alirkan' is a made-up word. It is understandable, but a native technical writer would not use it.

examples.source: Parameters are bound away. ... A PUB that still carries a parameter-values array fails coercion.
examples.translation: Parameter diikat terus. ... PUB yang masih membawa array nilai-parameter gagal dipaksa.
examples.suggested: Parameter dihapuskan melalui pengikatan. ... PUB yang masih membawa array nilai parameter akan gagal ditukar jenis (coercion).
examples.why: 'diikat terus' and 'gagal dipaksa' are literal renderings. They lose the idea that the parameters disappear and that type coercion fails.

editor_note: The rewritten method table in entry 11 keeps the meaning correct, including the blocking caveat on job.result() and "terminal state" as "keadaan akhir". Its terminology does not match the rest of the page, though. "Job" is rendered as "tugas" here, but every other entry uses "kerja", including the tab label and intro in entry 10 just before the table. Entry 20 also uses "tugas" for "task" in "tugas penyelenggaraan", so the two words blur. In the same way, "results" becomes "hasil" here but "keputusan" elsewhere on the page (entries 9, 13, 34, 38).

examples.source: Check the current job status / Get the unique job identifier / Block until the job reaches a terminal state
examples.translation: Semak status tugas semasa / Dapatkan pengecam tugas yang unik / Sekat sehingga tugas mencapai keadaan akhir
examples.suggested: Semak status kerja semasa / Dapatkan pengecam kerja yang unik / Sekat sehingga kerja mencapai keadaan akhir
examples.why: The rest of the file renders 'job' as 'kerja', and entry 20 uses 'tugas' for 'task'. Switching to 'tugas' only in this table is inconsistent and blurs the job/task distinction.

examples.source: Retrieve job results (blocking call until complete)
examples.translation: Dapatkan hasil tugas (panggilan menyekat sehingga selesai)
examples.suggested: Dapatkan semula keputusan kerja (panggilan menyekat sehingga selesai)
examples.why: Elsewhere on the page 'results' is 'keputusan' and 'retrieve' is 'dapatkan semula' (entries 9, 33-38). This row should use the same wording.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: "Semak API [`qiskit-ibm-runtime` Estimator/Sampler]" moves "API" to the front, which is correct Malay word order, and it matches the "Semak API [primitif ...]" pattern in entries 61-62.

Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning. "Mod" is the correct Malay statistical term for "mode", and "bilangan tertinggi" matches the Success Rate wording in the benchmark table (entry 27). The problem is the imperative verb. Entries 48 and 49 use the bare English-looking "Plot", but standard Malay writes "Plotkan" in instructions. A native editor would also change "adalah mod" to "ialah mod", because "ialah" is the usual copula before a noun phrase.

examples.source: **3. Plot the top bitstrings**
examples.translation: **3. Plot bitstring teratas**
examples.suggested: **3. Plotkan bitstring teratas**
examples.why: A bare 'Plot' reads as a leftover English verb. In Malay the imperative form is 'plotkan'.

examples.source: Plot the bitstring with the highest counts to see if the hidden bitstring was the mode.
examples.translation: Plot bitstring dengan bilangan tertinggi untuk melihat sama ada bitstring tersembunyi adalah mod.
examples.suggested: Plotkan bitstring dengan bilangan tertinggi untuk melihat sama ada bitstring tersembunyi ialah mod.
examples.why: 'Plotkan' is the proper imperative, and standard usage puts 'ialah' rather than 'adalah' before the noun 'mod'. The meaning is already faithful and 'mod' is correct for the statistical mode.

editor_note: Entry 141 is a faithful table: every score and version number matches the English, headers are idiomatic ("Metrik Penanda Aras", "Tarikh Keluaran", "Dilatih pada versi Qiskit"), and months are correctly localized (Januari, Jun, Februari).

All five rewritten entries (7, 20, 21, 33, 34) say the same thing as the English and nothing in them would mislead a learner. Entry 7 keeps the negation "tidak dapat melihat antara satu sama lain, walaupun mereka boleh mengakses sumber yang sama" intact, and "rantau us-east/eu-de" is the usual Malay cloud term for region. There are two small wording problems. In entry 7, "tugasan instans" reads as "instance task/homework"; for the act of assigning users to an instance, "penugasan instans" is the right word. In entry 21, "melakukan tindakan untuk bekerja dengan" copies the English wording and reads stiffly.

examples.source: regardless of instance assignment
examples.translation: tanpa mengira tugasan instans
examples.suggested: tanpa mengira penugasan instans
examples.why: 'Tugasan' usually means a task or assignment to be done, such as homework. 'Penugasan' is the act of assigning, which is what the English means here.

examples.source: allows users to perform actions to work with IBM Quantum service instances
examples.translation: membolehkan pengguna melakukan tindakan untuk bekerja dengan instans perkhidmatan IBM Quantum
examples.suggested: membolehkan pengguna melaksanakan tindakan pada instans perkhidmatan IBM Quantum
examples.why: 'Melakukan tindakan untuk bekerja dengan' copies the English phrasing word for word. A Malay technical writer would shorten it.

editor_note: The Malay is faithful and natural throughout, and the exam rules come through exactly: "sekurang-kurangnya 16 dengan betul untuk lulus" and "dikunci buat sementara waktu" after two failed attempts, with the standard "anda" register and "pembetulan ralat kuantum" used for "quantum error correction".

Rewritten entries 4, 5 and 7 are faithful and natural, keeping each caveat and the key negation: "qubit *logikal* yang tidak pernah terlepas daripada perlindungan", "nilai ambang terhingga tertentu", and "ia *tidak* bergantung pada saiz Circuit kuantum".

The meaning is faithful throughout. The 20-question exam, the 16-correct pass mark, the lock after two failed attempts and the Credly privacy notice all match the English. There are two small phrasing issues. In [10], "dalam beberapa hari ini" can read as "these (past) few days" rather than "the next few days", so "dalam beberapa hari akan datang" is clearer. In [7], "di mana anda boleh" copies the English relative "where", and Malay editors usually rewrite it as "untuk menduduki…" or "tempat anda boleh…".

examples.source: may be temporarily unavailable in the next few days
examples.translation: mungkin tidak tersedia buat sementara waktu dalam beberapa hari ini
examples.suggested: mungkin tidak tersedia buat sementara waktu dalam beberapa hari akan datang
examples.why: 'beberapa hari ini' is ambiguous and can mean the current or recent few days, while the source clearly means the upcoming days.

examples.source: navigate to IBM® Training, where you can take the badging exam
examples.translation: pergi ke IBM® Training, di mana anda boleh menduduki peperiksaan lencana
examples.suggested: pergi ke IBM® Training untuk menduduki peperiksaan lencana
examples.why: Using 'di mana' as a relative pronoun copies English grammar and is discouraged in standard Malay technical writing.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. Core terms are correct and used consistently: density matrices→matriks ketumpatan, channels→saluran, measurements→pengukuran, and quantum error correction→pembetulan ralat kuantum. The Credly/badge privacy paragraph keeps its full meaning.

I reviewed only the two rewritten entries. Both keep the English meaning and would not mislead a learner. In entry 16, "bersifat mekanikal kuantum secara semula jadi" says "in nature" twice, because "bersifat" already covers it; "secara semula jadi" is a literal copy of the English and should be dropped. In entry 17, "masalah minimasi" uses "minimasi", which reads as Indonesian. Standard Malay is "peminimuman", which also pairs with "Pengoptimuman" in the same line.

examples.source: Simulation of physical or chemical systems which are already quantum mechanical in nature.
examples.translation: Simulasi sistem fizikal atau kimia yang sudah bersifat mekanikal kuantum secara semula jadi.
examples.suggested: Simulasi sistem fizikal atau kimia yang sememangnya bersifat mekanikal kuantum.
examples.why: "bersifat" already means "in nature", so adding "secara semula jadi" says it twice. It is a literal copy of the English and reads stiffly.

examples.source: typically cast as minimizations problems.
examples.translation: yang biasanya dirumuskan sebagai masalah minimasi.
examples.suggested: yang biasanya dirumuskan sebagai masalah peminimuman.
examples.why: "minimasi" is an Indonesian-style borrowing. Standard Malay (DBP) uses "peminimuman", which matches "Pengoptimuman" in the same entry.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Entry 28 keeps both negations ("bukanlah keselarian eksponen", "bukan syarat yang mencukupi"), and entry 48 is a faithful True/False prompt, so its "Salah" answer still fits. One thing a native editor would still change: the rewrites translate "entangled" as "terbelit", but the rest of the page uses "berkait"/"keberkaitan" (entries 42 and 46). Entry 42 point 2 restates entry 28 almost word for word with "keadaan yang berkait", so a learner meets two different words for the same concept a few paragraphs apart. Pick one rendering and use it everywhere. The standard Malay term "keterjeratan"/"terjerat" would be the safest choice.

examples.source: High dimensionality of entangled quantum states is not exponential parallelism
examples.translation: Dimensi tinggi keadaan kuantum yang terbelit bukanlah keselarian eksponen
examples.suggested: Dimensi tinggi keadaan kuantum yang terjerat bukanlah keselarian eksponen
examples.why: Entry 42 point 2 restates this same claim as 'keadaan yang berkait', and entry 46 uses 'keberkaitan'. The two words for entanglement don't match; use one term (e.g. terjerat/keterjeratan) throughout.

examples.source: Highly entangled quantum states enable us to solve most machine learning problems
examples.translation: Keadaan kuantum yang sangat terbelit membolehkan kita menyelesaikan kebanyakan masalah
examples.suggested: Keadaan kuantum yang sangat terjerat membolehkan kita menyelesaikan kebanyakan masalah
examples.why: The meaning is faithful, but the 'entangled' term here doesn't match entries 42 and 46 (berkait/keberkaitan).

editor_note: The page's meaning holds up overall. The key teaching points survive intact: the 70/30 split, the +1/-1 labels, the horizontal-line reasoning in [53] and the 60% vs. 100% accuracy results. The main problem is terminology. "Variational" is rendered as "varian" (Malay for "variant") throughout, instead of "variasi". "Entanglement" becomes "penghubungan"/"menghubungkan" (connecting) in [19], [45] and [87], which in [19] reads like hardware connectivity, and [20] drops "entanglement" altogether. There are also calques: "forward pass" → "lulus ke hadapan" ("lulus" means passing an exam), "featureless" → "tidak berkesan" (ineffective), and "quantum speed-up" → "kelajuan kuantum". [74] also loosely rewords "logically matching the problem at hand".

examples.source: variational quantum classifiers (VQCs)
examples.translation: pengelas kuantum varian (VQC)
examples.suggested: pengelas kuantum variasi (VQC)
examples.why: 'varian' means 'variant'. 'Variasi' is the usual term for 'variational' (as in 'kaedah variasi'). The same rendering is used on every occurrence.

examples.source: Entangling adjacent qubits does not increase the depth by too much, but entangling very distant qubits
examples.translation: Menghubungkan qubit bersebelahan ... menghubungkan qubit yang sangat jauh
examples.suggested: Menjerat (mengkusutkan) qubit bersebelahan ... menjerat qubit yang sangat jauh
examples.why: 'Menghubungkan' means 'connecting', and in a paragraph about qubit layout it reads like physical connectivity. The idea of entanglement is lost.

examples.source: including entanglement and CNOT gates between qubits corresponding to adjacent pixels
examples.translation: memasukkan gate CNOT antara qubit yang sepadan dengan piksel bersebelahan
examples.suggested: memasukkan keterjeratan dan gate CNOT antara qubit yang sepadan dengan piksel bersebelahan
examples.why: The translation drops 'entanglement'.

examples.source: a function to run a forward pass
examples.translation: fungsi untuk menjalankan lulus ke hadapan
examples.suggested: fungsi untuk menjalankan hantaran ke hadapan (forward pass)
examples.why: 'Lulus' means passing a test. This is a literal calque of the ML term.

examples.source: becomes exponentially flat and featureless
examples.translation: menjadi rata dan tidak berkesan secara eksponen
examples.suggested: menjadi rata dan tanpa ciri secara eksponen
examples.why: 'Tidak berkesan' means 'ineffective', which changes the description of the landscape.

examples.source: expect a quantum speed-up
examples.translation: mengharapkan kelajuan kuantum
examples.suggested: mengharapkan pecutan kuantum
examples.why: 'Kelajuan' means 'speed', not 'speed-up'.

editor_note: All 17 rewritten entries keep the English meaning. The little-endian explanation (25), the unitary gate properties (38), the Z/X/Y basis rotation (71-72) and the glued-coin analogy (102) are accurate, and nothing is added that the source doesn't say. Two small slips remain. In entry 66, 'observable' is rendered as the adjective phrase 'boleh ukur' used as a noun, so the definition reads as 'a measurable quantity is called a measurable', which loses the point that this is a special technical term. 'cerapan' would be more idiomatic. Entry 38 also drops the preposition in 'vektor keadaan yang ia dikenakan', which reads as broken grammar.

examples.source: any measurable quantity is called an *observable*, and observables are represented by matrices
examples.translation: sebarang kuantiti yang boleh diukur dipanggil *boleh ukur*, dan boleh ukur diwakili oleh matriks
examples.suggested: sebarang kuantiti yang boleh diukur dipanggil *cerapan* (observable), dan cerapan diwakili oleh matriks
examples.why: The Malay sentence repeats the same adjective as its own definition, so the idea of a named technical term is lost. 'boleh ukur' is also awkward as a noun. The term is still recognizable, so this is minor.

examples.source: where $N$ is also the dimension of the state vector it is applied to
examples.translation: di mana $N$ juga adalah dimensi vektor keadaan yang ia dikenakan
examples.suggested: dengan $N$ juga ialah dimensi vektor keadaan yang dikenakan matriks tersebut
examples.why: The preposition is missing (it should say 'dikenakan kepadanya' or be rephrased), and the 'di mana' calque makes the clause read as ungrammatical.

editor_note: Entries 4 ("Mereka Bentuk dan Memimpin Projek Kuantum") and 6 ("Prinsip Asas Algoritma Kuantum") are faithful and natural. "Prinsip Asas" usefully keeps this title distinct from the "Asas ..." titles in entries 3, 5 and 9. Entry 12 renders "Diagonalization" as "Pempenjuruan", which is not a correct Malay word. The conventional DBP mathematics term is "pepenjuruan" (from "pepenjuru", diagonal). With the pem- prefix, the initial p would also elide. The word is still recognizable and does not mislead, so this is minor.

examples.source: [Quantum Diagonalization Algorithms](/learning/courses/quantum-diagonalization-algorithms)
examples.translation: [Algoritma Pempenjuruan Kuantum](/learning/courses/quantum-diagonalization-algorithms)
examples.suggested: [Algoritma Pepenjuruan Kuantum](/learning/courses/quantum-diagonalization-algorithms)
examples.why: 'Pempenjuruan' is not a correct Malay word. The standard DBP term for matrix diagonalization is 'pepenjuruan'. The current word is still recognizable, so this is minor.

editor_note: All six rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Terms are correct, for example "bilangan lelaran Grover yang optimum" (entry 120) and "Aliran kerja algoritma pertanyaan yang tepat" (entry 113). Entry 32 repeats the English typo "|+⟩ dan |+⟩" (it should be |−⟩ for the second state); that error is in the English source, not the translation.

Entries 4, 5 and 10 keep the English meaning, including the claim that activities take "jauh lebih singkat" than the free allotment and the simulator fallback caveat, so nothing here would mislead a learner. In entry 5, "independently" is rendered as "secara bebas", which reads more like "freely" than "on one's own". The contrast with "dalam kumpulan kecil" calls for "secara bersendirian" or "secara individu". Also in entry 5, the IBM product name "Open Plan" is translated as "Pelan Terbuka", so learners won't find it under that name on the IBM Quantum Platform. Keeping "Open Plan", or glossing it, would work better.

examples.source: but can be completed independently or in small groups
examples.translation: tetapi boleh disiapkan secara bebas atau dalam kumpulan kecil
examples.suggested: tetapi boleh disiapkan secara bersendirian atau dalam kumpulan kecil
examples.why: 'secara bebas' suggests 'freely/without restriction'. The English means working alone, set against group work.

examples.source: as part of the Open Plan available to all users
examples.translation: sebagai sebahagian daripada Pelan Terbuka yang tersedia untuk semua pengguna
examples.suggested: sebagai sebahagian daripada Open Plan (Pelan Terbuka) yang tersedia untuk semua pengguna
examples.why: 'Open Plan' is the name of an IBM Quantum plan. Translating it means learners can't match it to the platform's English UI.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the meaning of the English and would not mislead a learner. "Penyelesai Eigen Kuantum Variatif" is a sound Malay rendering. However, entries 4 and 197 now translate the expanded name, while the rest of the page still keeps it in English: "variational quantum eigensolver" in [0] and [70], and "Variational Quantum Eigensolver" in the [1] title and [69] heading. The algorithm's name should be written one way across the page. Entry 197 also uses "perolehi", a common non-standard form; standard Malay (DBP) is "peroleh".

examples.source: Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE)
examples.translation: Penyelesai Eigen Kuantum Variatif (VQE)
examples.suggested: Keep this rendering, but also use it in [0], [1], [69] and [70] (e.g. [69] 'VQE (Penyelesai Eigen Kuantum Variatif)'), or go back to the English name everywhere.
examples.why: The same algorithm is named two ways on one page: translated here and in [197], left in English in [0], [1], [69] and [70].

examples.source: Now let's use what we've obtained!
examples.translation: Sekarang mari gunakan apa yang kita perolehi!
examples.suggested: Sekarang mari kita gunakan apa yang telah kita peroleh!
examples.why: 'Perolehi' is a common non-standard form; DBP standard Malay is 'peroleh'. Adding 'kita'/'telah' also makes the sentence read more smoothly.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural: [57] renders "by hand" as "secara manual" and keeps "ketidakpastian" consistent with the rest of the page, and [116] "membawa ini ke had mutlaknya, dengan menjadikan ⟨Y⟩ sebesar mungkin" keeps the "absolute limit / as large as possible" intent.

All three rewritten entries (124, 125, 127) keep their meaning. The CNOT argument order, Qiskit's |q1q0> ket convention, A=q0 as control and B=q1 as target with the control on the right, and "b flips when a=1" all match the English. Two small wording fixes remain. The adjacent new entries render "gate" two ways: "Argumen gate" in [124] but "get ini" in [125]. They should use one form, and "get" is the one the surrounding CNOT section uses. In [127], "bertukar (dibalikkan)" hedges between two verbs in parentheses; a native editor would keep just "dibalikkan", the verb the page already uses for "flipped" in [150].

examples.source: The gate arguments are ordered as $CNOT(q_{control},q_{target})$
examples.translation: Argumen gate disusun sebagai $CNOT(q_{control},q_{target})$
examples.suggested: Argumen get disusun sebagai $CNOT(q_{control},q_{target})$
examples.why: The very next entry [125] uses "get ini", so two neighbouring rewritten entries render the same term differently.

examples.source: while the target value $b$ flips when $a=1$.
examples.translation: manakala nilai sasaran $b$ bertukar (dibalikkan) apabila $a=1$.
examples.suggested: manakala nilai sasaran $b$ dibalikkan apabila $a=1$.
examples.why: The two verbs with one in parentheses read as translator hedging. "dibalikkan" alone is clear and matches the Toffoli entry [150].

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally; key passages keep their meaning, including "jauh lebih singkat daripada masa percuma yang diperuntukkan" for the Open Plan time limit, "kunci jawapan" for "answer keys" and "mekanik kuantum peringkat ijazah pertama" for "undergraduate quantum mechanics".

Entry 49 is faithful: the aligned particles still go to the stronger side and the anti-aligned ones to the weaker side, as in the English. 'pesongan maksimum' fits 'pesongan' used elsewhere on the page, and 'sejajar bertentangan' matches the rendering of anti-aligned in entry 38.

All three rewritten entries say what the English says: "Petakan kepada masalah kuantum" [4], "Tetapkan Hamiltonian dan observable masalah kita" [5] and "Gunakan backend palsu demi kesederhanaan" [14].

Of the five rewritten entries, four are accurate: [13], [20], [21] and [40]. Entry [20] keeps the reset-then-SWAP equivalence, the source/destination roles and the entanglement caveat ("runtuh separa"). The one problem is in entry [36]. There, "taburan kuasi-kebarangkalian bersama gate yang didekomposisi" can be read with "bersama" meaning "together with", so a reader could take the subexperiments to come from the distribution "together with the decomposed gates" rather than from the gates' joint distribution. Adding "bagi" removes the ambiguity. It is recoverable from context, so it is not a FAIL.

examples.source: generated from the decomposed gates' joint quasiprobability distribution
examples.translation: dijana daripada taburan kuasi-kebarangkalian bersama gate yang didekomposisi
examples.suggested: dijana daripada taburan kuasi-kebarangkalian bersama bagi gate yang didekomposisi
examples.why: Without 'bagi', 'bersama' reads as the preposition 'together with' instead of the adjective 'joint'. That blurs whose distribution it is.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The slice counts (7, 3 more, 10), the limit of 8 Pauli groups, the 5e-3 per-slice error budget and the 1e-4 error all match the English. The main term problem is that operator "terms" is rendered as "istilah", which means a vocabulary term; the mathematical word is "sebutan". "Instance" is rendered as "contoh", which means "example", in [32] and [49]. There are also inconsistencies: "error budget" is "belanjawan ralat" in [38]-[40] but "bajet ralat" in [41], "how-to guide" is "panduan cara-untuk" but also "cara-buat", and the reader is addressed as "kamu" in [15]/[36] but "anda" in [41].

examples.source: at the cost of additional terms in the operator
examples.translation: dengan kos tambahan istilah dalam operator tersebut
examples.suggested: dengan kos sebutan tambahan dalam operator tersebut
examples.why: 'istilah' means a vocabulary term. For the terms of a Pauli sum the standard Malay mathematical word is 'sebutan'. The same issue appears in [3], [32], [35], [38] and [48].

examples.source: pass the backend instance into the constructor
examples.translation: menghantar contoh Backend ke dalam konstruktor
examples.suggested: menghantar objek (tika) Backend ke dalam konstruktor
examples.why: 'contoh' means 'example', not an object instance. The same issue appears in [32] ('contoh OperatorBudget').

examples.source: distributing an error budget across your slices, check out this how-to guide
examples.translation: pengagihan bajet ralat merentas kepingan anda, lihat [panduan cara-buat ini]
examples.suggested: pengagihan belanjawan ralat merentas kepingan anda, lihat [panduan cara-untuk ini]
examples.why: This entry uses 'bajet' and 'cara-buat', but the rest of the file uses 'belanjawan' and 'cara-untuk'. It also says 'anda', while [15] and [36] use 'kamu'.

examples.source: without allowing the operator to grow too large
examples.translation: tanpa membiarkan operator membesar terlalu besar
examples.suggested: tanpa membiarkan operator menjadi terlalu besar
examples.why: 'membesar terlalu besar' repeats the same root word and reads as a calque. The same phrasing appears in [3].

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the long caveats in [69] and [94] and the per-method recommendations, and nothing would mislead a learner. There are a few terminology problems. Transpilation is rendered as "Pentransformatan" in the link titles [11]/[13] but as "transpilasi" everywhere else, and "pass manager" appears both left in English [13] and as "pengurus laluan" elsewhere. Fidelity is rendered as "ketepatan" (accuracy) instead of "fideliti/kesetiaan". Smaller slips: [74] opens with "Walaupun" ("although") where it means "even", which turns the sentence into a fragment. [61] makes "noticeably slower" stronger as "jauh lebih perlahan". [87] has the calque "dua prestasi terkuat".

examples.source: [Transpilation concepts](/guides/transpile)
examples.translation: [Konsep Pentransformatan](/guides/transpile)
examples.suggested: [Konsep Transpilasi](/guides/transpile)
examples.why: 'Pentransformatan' means generic transformation. The rest of the file uses 'transpilasi', so this is inconsistent and less precise.

examples.source: Even modest differences in depth and gate count translate into measurable differences in fidelity under the depolarizing noise model.
examples.translation: Walaupun perbezaan kecil dalam kedalaman dan bilangan gate menghasilkan perbezaan ketepatan yang boleh diukur di bawah model hingar depolarisasi.
examples.suggested: Malah perbezaan kecil dalam kedalaman dan bilangan gate pun menghasilkan perbezaan fideliti yang boleh diukur di bawah model hingar depolarisasi.
examples.why: 'Walaupun' means 'although', which makes the sentence a dangling subordinate clause. 'Ketepatan' (accuracy) is also a loose rendering of fidelity.

examples.source: This is often the bottleneck for fidelity on real hardware.
examples.translation: Ini sering menjadi kesesakan bagi ketepatan pada perkakasan sebenar.
examples.suggested: Ini sering menjadi faktor pengehad utama bagi fideliti pada perkakasan sebenar.
examples.why: Fidelity is a specific quantum metric, and 'ketepatan' means accuracy. 'Kesesakan' (congestion) is also a stiff calque of 'bottleneck'.

examples.source: while the AI-powered transpiler is noticeably slower on certain circuits.
examples.translation: manakala transpiler berkuasa AI jauh lebih perlahan pada litar tertentu.
examples.suggested: manakala transpiler berkuasa AI ketara lebih perlahan pada litar tertentu.
examples.why: 'Jauh lebih' (much slower) makes the claim slightly stronger than 'noticeably'.

examples.source: SABRE and the AI-powered transpiler are the two strongest performers
examples.translation: SABRE dan transpiler berkuasa AI adalah dua prestasi terkuat
examples.suggested: SABRE dan transpiler berkuasa AI ialah dua kaedah berprestasi terbaik
examples.why: This calque calls the methods 'performances' rather than performers.

editor_note: All six rewritten entries (14, 15, 16, 17, 32, 49) say what the English says. The conditional X/Z corrections, the lower-MSE-means-higher-fidelity rule and the CDF axis description all match, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The problems are wording and terminology. "Mid-circuit measurement" is written three ways: "pengukuran pertengahan litar" in [14], "pengukuran litar tengah" in [32] and "pengukuran pertengahan-litar" in [49]. MSE is "min kuasa dua ralat" in [17], a word-order calque, but "ralat min kuasa dua" in [41]. Decoherence is misspelled "Penyahaskoheranan" in [15]. Entanglement moves between "pembelitan" in [14] and "keterikatan" in [49], and [49] uses the colloquial "bising" for noisy where the rest of the page uses "hingar".

examples.source: Qubit decoherence during the necessary delay
examples.translation: Penyahaskoheranan qubit semasa kelewatan yang diperlukan
examples.suggested: Penyahkoherenan qubit semasa kelewatan yang diperlukan
examples.why: 'Penyahaskoheranan' is not a real word. The standard term for decoherence is 'penyahkoherenan' (or 'dekoherens').

examples.source: We use the mean squared error (MSE) of these stabilizers
examples.translation: Kita gunakan min kuasa dua ralat (MSE) penstabil ini
examples.suggested: Kita gunakan ralat min kuasa dua (MSE) bagi penstabil ini
examples.why: This reverses the conventional Malay word order, and entry [41] on the same page correctly uses 'ralat min kuasa dua'.

examples.source: Mid-circuit measurements and feedforward
examples.translation: Pengukuran litar tengah dan suapan ke hadapan (feedforward)
examples.suggested: Pengukuran pertengahan litar dan suapan ke hadapan (feedforward)
examples.why: 'Litar tengah' reads as 'middle circuit'. It also clashes with 'pengukuran pertengahan litar' in [14] and 'pertengahan-litar' in [49], so the page has three renderings of one term.

examples.source: and communicate measurement results classically to link distant qubits
examples.translation: dan berkomunikasi hasil pengukuran secara klasik
examples.suggested: dan menyampaikan hasil pengukuran secara klasik
examples.why: 'Berkomunikasi' cannot take a direct object, so this is ungrammatical. The informal 'tapi' earlier in the same entry should also be 'tetapi' in documentation prose.

examples.source: if one chain includes a particularly noisy readout qubit
examples.translation: jika satu rantai mengandungi qubit pembacaan yang sangat bising
examples.suggested: jika satu rantai mengandungi qubit pembacaan yang sangat berhingar
examples.why: 'Bising' is everyday loudness. The page otherwise uses 'hingar' for quantum noise. In the same entry, 'order magnitud' should be 'tertib magnitud' and 'keterikatan' departs from 'pembelitan' in [14].

examples.source: (call this bit $m_{12}$) ... should ideally be entangled
examples.translation: (panggil bit ini $m_{12}$) ... seharusnya secara idealnya terikat
examples.suggested: (namakan bit ini $m_{12}$) ... sepatutnya, secara ideal, terikat
examples.why: 'Panggil bit ini' is a word-for-word calque, and 'seharusnya secara idealnya' repeats the same idea twice.

editor_note: The physics and the numbers carry over correctly: 0.3π and 0.5π, 21×12=252 circuits, 125/144 qubits, and the direction the critical point shifts all match the source. The weak spots are word-sense errors in key terms. "Long-range order" becomes "perintah jarak jauh" (perintah means "command") in [42], [58] and [62], even though [16] correctly says "fasa teratur". Magnetization is rendered as "magnet" rather than "pemagnetan", and "override" as "menolak" ("reject") in [52]. Smaller slips: "gandinggan" is a typo for "gandingan"; the interpreter is called "penterjemah" instead of "pentafsir"; "run" is used as a noun in the form "jalankan" ([68], [74]); "resolve" becomes "diselesaikan"; routing appears as both "melaraskan" and "penghalaan" in [51]; and "software package" is left in English in [82].

examples.source: the long-range order can still be recovered up until a critical angle
examples.translation: perintah jarak jauh masih boleh dipulihkan sehingga sudut kritikal
examples.suggested: tertib jarak jauh masih boleh dipulihkan sehingga sudut kritikal
examples.why: 'perintah' means command or instruction, not physical ordering. It also clashes with 'fasa teratur jarak jauh' in [16]. The same error recurs in [58] and [62].

examples.source: The layout and routing stages are already overridden by default to do nothing ... you can override or pass additional options
examples.translation: Peringkat susun atur dan penghalaan sudah ditolak lalainya ... anda boleh menolak atau menghantar pilihan tambahan
examples.suggested: Secara lalai, peringkat susun atur dan penghalaan telah diganti supaya tidak melakukan apa-apa ... anda boleh mengatasi atau menghantar pilihan tambahan
examples.why: 'menolak' reads as 'reject', so the sentence says you can reject options instead of overriding them.

examples.source: plotting the magnetization of the measured bitstrings
examples.translation: memplot magnet rentetan bit yang diukur
examples.suggested: memplot pemagnetan rentetan bit yang diukur
examples.why: 'magnet' means a physical magnet. The quantity is 'pemagnetan', and the same substitution appears in [59], [60] and [64] ('magnet kuasadua').

examples.source: In the runs above ... the transition is at the edge of what this sweep can resolve
examples.translation: Dalam jalankan di atas ... di pinggiran apa yang boleh diselesaikan oleh sapuan ini
examples.suggested: Dalam larian di atas ... di pinggiran apa yang dapat dibezakan oleh sapuan ini
examples.why: The verb 'jalankan' is used as a noun, which is ungrammatical, and 'diselesaikan' means 'solved', not 'resolved' in the measurement sense.

examples.source: cause the interpreter to hang until the jobs are finished
examples.translation: menyebabkan penterjemah berhenti sehingga kerja-kerja selesai
examples.suggested: menyebabkan pentafsir tersekat sehingga kerja-kerja selesai
examples.why: 'penterjemah' is a human translator. A Python interpreter is 'pentafsir'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the variational-bound, M_J-at-product-stage and qubit-excitation arguments, so this would not mislead a learner. The problem is terminology: it switches convention around entry [105], as if two translators worked on it. Before that point, and after it: shell is cengkerang then kelompok, diagonalization is pepenjuruan then diagonalisasi, shot is tembakan then shot, register is daftar then register, pool is kumpulan then kolam, pooled is terkumpul then berkumpul, budget is bajet then belanjawan, product is hasil darab then produk, two-body is dua-jasad then dua-badan, and ground state is keadaan-asas then keadaan-dasar. keadaan-asas (ground state) also nearly collides with keadaan asas (basis states) in [13]/[142]. There are also small slips: 'dilepasi' for 'passed' as an argument, 'memberikan sedikit penambahbaikan' reads softer than 'offers little improvement', and two link texts are left in English ([Background], [Setup]).

examples.source: Parity is *automatically* satisfied inside a single major shell
examples.translation: Pariti *secara automatik* dipenuhi di dalam satu kelompok major
examples.suggested: Pariti *secara automatik* dipenuhi di dalam satu cengkerang utama
examples.why: Earlier entries render 'shell' as 'cengkerang' (model-cengkerang, cengkerang $sd$). From [107] on it becomes 'kelompok' ('group/cluster'), and 'major' is left as an English calque. The same second-half split affects diagonalisasi/pepenjuruan, register/daftar, kolam/kumpulan and belanjawan/bajet.

examples.source: a rigorous upper bound on the true ground-state energy
examples.translation: sempadan atas yang tegar bagi tenaga keadaan-dasar sebenar
examples.suggested: sempadan atas yang tegar bagi tenaga keadaan-asas sebenar (or use keadaan dasar consistently throughout)
examples.why: 'Ground state' is keadaan-asas in [22]/[64] but keadaan-dasar here and in [135]/[168]. keadaan-asas also sits close to 'keadaan asas' = basis states in [13]/[142], so one consistent, distinct term is needed.

examples.source: adding more of the retained determinants offers little improvement
examples.translation: menambah lebih banyak penentu yang dikekalkan memberikan sedikit penambahbaikan
examples.suggested: menambah lebih banyak penentu yang dikekalkan hanya memberikan sedikit penambahbaikan
examples.why: 'Sedikit' on its own can read as 'some improvement'. Adding 'hanya' restores the English sense of diminishing returns.

examples.source: Every argument is passed as *twice* its physical value
examples.translation: Setiap hujah dilepasi sebagai *dua kali* nilai fizikalnya
examples.suggested: Setiap argumen dihantar sebagai *dua kali* nilai fizikalnya
examples.why: 'Dilepasi' means 'passed through/exceeded', not 'passed' as a function argument. 'Hujah' is the rhetorical sense of 'argument'.

examples.source: the register information from the [Background](#background)
examples.translation: maklumat daftar daripada [Background](#background)
examples.suggested: maklumat daftar daripada [Latar belakang](#background)
examples.why: The link text is left in English here (and [Setup] in [98]), while [104] and [163] translate the same links.

editor_note: None of the 13 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The optimization_level=0 caveat in [77], the noise scale of 0.0 in [136] and the PNA/TREX/PS conclusions in [149]-[153] all match the English. The remaining problems are phrasing. [81] says 'melangkaui lebih daripada sekadar', which doubles up 'goes beyond'. [140] starts its list of steps with 'mencipta' and then switches to the bare forms 'sediakan'/'jalankan'. [150] renders 'randomized circuits' as 'litar rawakisasi', but the rest of the page uses 'litar rawak'. The heading [139] uses the verb-noun form 'Mempersampelkan', while the other step headings are imperatives ('Pelajari', 'Nyatakan').

examples.source: which goes beyond simply identifying two-qubit layers
examples.translation: yang melangkaui lebih daripada sekadar mengenal pasti lapisan dua-qubit
examples.suggested: yang melakukan lebih daripada sekadar mengenal pasti lapisan dua-qubit
examples.why: 'Melangkaui' already means 'goes beyond', so adding 'lebih daripada' says it twice.

examples.source: We simply instantiate the `Executor` object, provide it with the backend, and run the program.
examples.translation: Kita hanya perlu mencipta instans objek `Executor`, sediakan backend kepadanya, dan jalankan program tersebut.
examples.suggested: Kita hanya perlu mencipta instans objek `Executor`, menyediakan backend kepadanya, dan menjalankan program tersebut.
examples.why: The three steps use mismatched verb forms: 'mencipta' has the meN- prefix, but 'sediakan' and 'jalankan' are bare imperatives.

examples.source: sampling imbalance in the randomized circuits
examples.translation: ketidakseimbangan persampelan dalam litar rawakisasi
examples.suggested: ketidakseimbangan persampelan dalam litar rawak
examples.why: 'Litar rawakisasi' reads as 'randomization circuits', and the rest of the file uses 'litar rawak' for randomized circuits.

examples.source: Sample the circuit using the `Executor`
examples.translation: Mempersampelkan litar menggunakan `Executor`
examples.suggested: Sampelkan litar menggunakan `Executor`
examples.why: The other step headings use imperatives ('Pelajari hingar', 'Nyatakan cara'), but this one uses a verb-noun form.

editor_note: The rewritten entry 15 keeps the meaning of the English. The fuel and material-waste examples, "Hamiltonian kos", "penyelesaian calon" and the caveat about needing a suitable objective and constraints (kekangan) are all carried over faithfully, so it would not mislead a learner. One thing to fix: it renders "combinatorial optimization" as "Pengoptimuman kombinatorik". Entries 6 and 14 of the same page use "pengoptimuman kombinatorial". Change it to "kombinatorial" so the term is the same across the file.

examples.source: Combinatorial optimization also appears in sustainability challenges
examples.translation: Pengoptimuman kombinatorik juga muncul dalam cabaran kemampanan
examples.suggested: Pengoptimuman kombinatorial juga muncul dalam cabaran kemampanan
examples.why: Entries 6 and 14 use 'pengoptimuman kombinatorial'. This entry is the only place that uses 'kombinatorik', which makes the page inconsistent.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The physics holds up, including the J normalization caveat in [28], the zero-magnetization argument in [32] and the fidelity explanation in [72]. I found no drift or hallucination. The problems are editorial. "Approximate quantum compiling" is rendered as "pengkompilan kuantum anggaran" in [6] but as "penyusunan kuantum anggaran" everywhere else. Several phrases are calques: "kita berdagang ketepatan dengan kos pengiraan" for "trade off" in [40], "mula-panas" for "warm-starts" in [62], and the clumsy "menjelmakan-Fourier ia" in [12]. In [86], "deployed" is weakened to "yang digunakan".

examples.source: approximate quantum compiling (AQC)
examples.translation: pengkompilan kuantum anggaran (AQC)
examples.suggested: penyusunan kuantum anggaran (AQC)
examples.why: The rest of the file ([11], [37], [38], [57], [89]) uses 'penyusunan kuantum anggaran', so the term should be the same here.

examples.source: we trade off accuracy against computational cost
examples.translation: kita berdagang ketepatan dengan kos pengiraan
examples.suggested: kita mengimbangi ketepatan dengan kos pengiraan
examples.why: 'Berdagang' means commercial trading, so this is a literal calque of 'trade off'. 'Mengimbangi' (to balance) is the natural wording.

examples.source: each step warm-starts from the previous step's optimized parameters
examples.translation: setiap langkah mula-panas daripada parameter yang dioptimumkan langkah sebelumnya
examples.suggested: setiap langkah dimulakan dengan parameter teroptimum daripada langkah sebelumnya
examples.why: 'Mula-panas' is a word-for-word calque of 'warm-start' and does not read as natural Malay.

examples.source: Fourier-transform it into a DSF
examples.translation: menjelmakan-Fourier ia menjadi DSF
examples.suggested: menukarkannya kepada DSF melalui jelmaan Fourier
examples.why: The hyphenated verb followed by 'ia' as an object copies English syntax. Malay would attach the object with the suffix '-nya'.

examples.source: a deployed Qiskit Serverless function template
examples.translation: templat fungsi Qiskit Serverless yang digunakan
examples.suggested: templat fungsi Qiskit Serverless yang telah dilancarkan
examples.why: 'Yang digunakan' means 'used', so the sense of a template that is already deployed is lost.

editor_note: None of the 13 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The epsilon=0.5 reduction to standard QAOA, the tight QP relaxation, the approximation-ratio direction and the "got lucky" caveat all carry over faithfully. The problems are editorial. Entry 67 renders "noisier hardware" as "perkakasan yang lebih bising", which clashes with "berhingar"/"bebas hingar" used elsewhere on the page (entries 16, 54). Entry 57 calques "ground-truth reference" as "rujukan kebenaran asas" and uses the non-standard "minimumasi" instead of "peminimuman". Entries 0 and 40 have stiff doubled connectives ("dengan memulakan dengan", "yang mendasari yang dikembalikan").

examples.source: On harder problems, noisier hardware, or with more candidate solutions competing
examples.translation: Pada masalah yang lebih sukar, perkakasan yang lebih bising, atau ...
examples.suggested: Pada masalah yang lebih sukar, perkakasan yang lebih berhingar, atau ...
examples.why: 'bising' means acoustic loudness. Elsewhere this page uses 'hingar' for quantum noise ('berhingar' in entry 16, 'bebas hingar' in entry 54), so 67 should match.

examples.source: For minimization problems ... serves as a ground-truth reference.
examples.translation: Untuk masalah minimumasi ... berfungsi sebagai rujukan kebenaran asas.
examples.suggested: Untuk masalah peminimuman ... berfungsi sebagai rujukan sebenar (ground truth).
examples.why: 'kebenaran asas' is a word-for-word calque of 'ground truth' that a Malay reader would not recognise. 'minimumasi' is not standard; DBP usage is 'peminimuman'.

examples.source: by initializing with the solution of a continuous relaxation
examples.translation: dengan memulakan dengan penyelesaian relaksasi selanjar
examples.suggested: dengan memulakannya menggunakan penyelesaian relaksasi selanjar
examples.why: Repeating 'dengan' back to back is clunky translationese.

examples.source: The underlying `OptimizationProblem` returned by `to_optimization_problem()`
examples.translation: `OptimizationProblem` yang mendasari yang dikembalikan oleh `to_optimization_problem()`
examples.suggested: `OptimizationProblem` asas yang dikembalikan oleh `to_optimization_problem()`
examples.why: Two 'yang' clauses in a row make the English structure show through. One adjective reads more naturally.

editor_note: None of the 35 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The CNOT control/target logic (entry 81), the X-gate p→1-p claim (56) and the Sampler/Estimator descriptions (105) all match the English. The remaining problems are wording and consistency. "Plot the result" is rendered "memetakan hasilnya" (to map) in entry 5, while entry 110 correctly uses "memplot". Multi-qubit gates are named three ways: "Gate Berbilang Qubit" (76), "multi-qubit gate" (77, 79) and "single-qubit gate" left in English next to "gate satu-Qubit" (61). "Cloud" is "awan" in entry 10 but stays "cloud" in 108. "Observables" appears as the unusual hyphenated coinage "boleh-cerapan" (105).

examples.source: Run you circuits on the real quantum computer and plot the result.
examples.translation: Menjalankan litar anda pada komputer kuantum sebenar dan memetakan hasilnya.
examples.suggested: Menjalankan litar anda pada komputer kuantum sebenar dan memplot hasilnya.
examples.why: 'Memetakan' means 'to map', not 'to plot'. Entry 110 already uses 'memplot', so this also makes the file inconsistent.

examples.source: Now that you've understood the single-qubit gates, let us look at gates operating on multiple qubits... combining single-qubit gates and multi-qubit gates.
examples.translation: Setelah anda memahami single-qubit gate, ... dengan menggabungkan single-qubit gate dan multi-qubit gate.
examples.suggested: Setelah anda memahami gate satu qubit, ... dengan menggabungkan gate satu qubit dan gate berbilang qubit.
examples.why: The heading in entry 76 says 'Gate Berbilang Qubit' and entry 61 says 'gate satu-Qubit', but this entry keeps the English compounds. The page names the same concepts inconsistently.

examples.source: In case of there are many waiting queue at the cloud
examples.translation: Sekiranya ada banyak giliran menunggu di cloud
examples.suggested: Sekiranya barisan menunggu di awan panjang
examples.why: Entry 10 renders 'cloud' as 'awan', so leaving it in English here is inconsistent. 'Banyak giliran menunggu' is also a word-for-word copy of the broken English.

examples.source: computes the expectation value of one or more observables
examples.translation: mengira nilai jangkaan satu atau lebih boleh-cerapan
examples.suggested: mengira nilai jangkaan satu atau lebih cerapan (observable)
examples.why: The hyphenated 'boleh-cerapan' is an odd, unusual coinage. A more conventional term, or 'cerapan' with the English in brackets, would be clearer to learners.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The gate descriptions, the probabilities and the Bell/GHZ exercises all match the English. The problems are in wording. The page uses casual "kamu" throughout instead of "anda", and from [77] on it drifts into colloquial speech ("dah", "jom", "nak", "tengok", "tak"). A few words are malformed or calqued: the hybrid "dinoted" in [82], the Qiskit-pattern step "Optima" in [98] (should be the verb "Optimumkan"), and "gangguan" for quantum interference in [47], where the physics term is "interferens". Circuit is also rendered inconsistently: "litar kuantum" in [101] but "Circuit" everywhere else.

examples.source: the resulting state is denoted by $|\Phi^+\rangle$
examples.translation: keadaan yang terhasil dinoted sebagai $|\Phi^+\rangle$
examples.suggested: keadaan yang terhasil ditandakan sebagai $|\Phi^+\rangle$
examples.why: 'dinoted' is an English verb with a Malay prefix stuck on, not a Malay word.

examples.source: **Optimize** for target hardware
examples.translation: **Optima** untuk perkakasan sasaran
examples.suggested: **Optimumkan** untuk perkakasan sasaran
examples.why: 'Optima' is not an imperative verb. The parallel steps 'Peta' and 'Laksana' read as verbs, so this step should be 'Optimumkan'.

examples.source: the quantum phase is what enables interference between quantum states
examples.translation: fasa kuantum adalah yang membolehkan gangguan antara keadaan kuantum
examples.suggested: fasa kuantum ialah perkara yang membolehkan interferens antara keadaan kuantum
examples.why: 'gangguan' means disturbance or noise. The standard Malay physics term for wave or quantum interference is 'interferens'.

examples.source: Now that you've understood the single-qubit gates, let us look at gates operating on multiple qubits.
examples.translation: Sekarang yang kamu dah faham gate satu-Qubit, jom kita tengok gate yang beroperasi pada berbilang qubit.
examples.suggested: Sekarang setelah anda memahami gate satu qubit, mari kita lihat gate yang beroperasi pada berbilang qubit.
examples.why: Colloquial 'dah/jom/tengok' and 'kamu' break the standard 'anda' register used in technical documentation. The same slang recurs in [79], [94], [103], [108] and [110].

examples.source: by building quantum circuits to generate the desired quantum state
examples.translation: dengan membina litar kuantum untuk menjana keadaan kuantum yang dikehendaki
examples.suggested: Use the same rendering as the rest of the file
examples.why: Only this entry uses 'litar'. Every other entry keeps 'Circuit', so the term is inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: Entry [6] renders "Qiskit advocate program" as "Program peguam Qiskit" ("Qiskit lawyer program"), which misstates what the community ambassador programme is. In [64], "running the circuit many times" became "beberapa kali" ("a few times"). That weakens the core point about sampling that the shots discussion depends on. "Observable" is split between "pemerhatian" ("observation", in [36], [54] and [55]/[56]) and the English "observable" ([61], [64]). "Qiskit Patterns" also appears both untranslated and as "corak Qiskit". The page uses casual "kamu" throughout except "anda" in heading [16], where the standard is "anda".

examples.source: [Qiskit advocate program](...)
examples.translation: [Program peguam Qiskit](...)
examples.suggested: [Program Qiskit Advocate](...) / [Program duta Qiskit](...)
examples.why: 'peguam' means lawyer; this mistranslation tells the learner it is a legal/lawyer programme rather than a community advocate programme.

examples.source: you usually collect a sample of the outputs by running the circuit many times
examples.translation: biasanya kamu kumpul sampel output dengan menjalankan Circuit beberapa kali
examples.suggested: biasanya anda kumpul sampel output dengan menjalankan litar berkali-kali / banyak kali
examples.why: 'beberapa kali' means 'a few times', which weakens the claim; sampling needs many repetitions (shots).

examples.source: *operators* represent the observables to be measured
examples.translation: *operator* mewakili pemerhatian yang akan diukur
examples.suggested: *operator* mewakili cerapan (observable) yang akan diukur
examples.why: 'pemerhatian' means 'observation', not the operator concept, and later entries [61] and [64] use 'observable', so the term is inconsistent.

examples.source: Set up your IBM Quantum Platform account
examples.translation: Sediakan akaun IBM Quantum Platform anda
examples.suggested: Use 'anda' consistently across the page (the body uses 'kamu')
examples.why: The page mixes registers: casual 'kamu' is used everywhere except this heading, where the convention is standard 'anda'.

editor_note: None of the 12 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The percentages, bitstrings, qubit ordering (entry 32) and criterion numbers in entries 12 and 82 all match the English. The remaining problems are terminology consistency and naturalness. Entry 82 renders "entangling" as "menjerat", while the rest of the page uses "terbelit/belitan". Entry 25 renders "fidelity" as "kesetiaan", while entries 15, 26 and 80 use "ketepatan". Entry 22 mixes "simulator bising" and "persekitaran hingar" in one sentence. Entry 12 ends with a calque, "membolehkan eksperimen dengan mereka", which uses "mereka" for the criteria (non-human). Entry 4 leaves "secara hands-on" in English.

examples.source: and entangling distant qubits (Criteria 6 & 7)
examples.translation: dan menjerat qubit yang berjauhan (Kriteria 6 & 7)
examples.suggested: dan membelitkan qubit yang berjauhan (Kriteria 6 & 7)
examples.why: 'Jerat' (keterjeratan) is a recognised Malay term for entanglement, but everywhere else on this page it is 'terbelit/belitan'. Read on its own, 'menjerat' can also mean 'trapping'.

examples.source: maintaining high fidelity gets harder without error correction
examples.translation: mengekalkan kesetiaan tinggi menjadi lebih sukar tanpa pembetulan ralat
examples.suggested: mengekalkan ketepatan yang tinggi menjadi lebih sukar tanpa pembetulan ralat
examples.why: Elsewhere on the page, 'fidelity' is 'ketepatan' (entries 15, 26 and 80). Using 'kesetiaan' here splits the term.

examples.source: on a noisy simulator ... in a realistic noise environment
examples.translation: pada simulator bising ... dalam persekitaran hingar yang realistik
examples.suggested: pada simulator berhingar ... dalam persekitaran hingar yang realistik
examples.why: 'Noise' is rendered two ways (bising/hingar) within one short paragraph. Pick 'hingar' consistently.

examples.source: what each DiVincenzo criterion means in practice and how Qiskit enables experimenting with them
examples.translation: apa yang setiap kriteria DiVincenzo bermaksud dalam amalan dan bagaimana Qiskit membolehkan eksperimen dengan mereka
examples.suggested: maksud setiap kriteria DiVincenzo dalam amalan dan bagaimana Qiskit membolehkan kita bereksperimen dengannya
examples.why: The word order is calqued from the English, and 'mereka' is a human pronoun used here for the criteria.

examples.source: to **explore each principle hands-on**
examples.translation: untuk **meneroka setiap prinsip secara hands-on**
examples.suggested: untuk **meneroka setiap prinsip secara langsung/amali**
examples.why: 'Hands-on' is left in English, although entries 72 and 75 on the same page render it as 'langsung'.
